title: Best Speechwriters for Hire (2026): Wedding and Event Speeches
description: How to hire a speechwriter for weddings, business events, conferences or toasts: length, voice, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Speechwriters help you say the right thing in front of an audience: a wedding toast, a eulogy, a keynote, a company announcement or an award speech. A good speech sounds like you, fits the time you have and leaves people with one clear feeling or idea. Speeches go wrong when they are too long, full of phrases you would never say, or missing the stories only you know. This guide helps you get a speech you can deliver with confidence.

faq.q: How long should my speech be?
faq.a: Shorter than you think. Many personal speeches work best at a few minutes. Ask the organizer how much time you have and give that limit to the writer.
Share how you talk: a voice note, emails or a past speech. Read the draft aloud and ask for changes wherever it does not feel natural.

faq.q: What information does the writer need?
faq.a: The occasion, audience, your relationship to the people involved, key stories and anything to avoid.
Some writers add notes on pauses and emphasis or offer coaching. Ask if you want help practicing.
Agree that the writer will not share your speech or personal stories without permission.
